title: Manus raises more than $500 million after Meta exit
source_used: TechCrunch (same story as the Reuters headline; reuters.com returns 401), cross-checked with The Next Web
key_facts: Butterfly Effect, parent company of the AI agent startup Manus, said in a WeChat post on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that it raised more than $500 million.
It is the first funding round since Meta was forced to call off its $2 billion acquisition of Manus.
Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led; Tencent, HSG (formerly Sequoia China), ZhenFund and others also took part.
Valuation was not disclosed; last month Manus was said to be in talks at about a $4 billion valuation.
Manus moved its staff to Singapore in mid-2025; Meta announced the deal in December 2025; Chinese authorities ordered it unwound in April 2026.
Manus resumed independent operations in August and said it had to delete some user data as part of the split.
The company is reported to be considering a Hong Kong listing.
quote_evidence: Chinese AI lab Manus’ parent company, Butterfly Effect, said on Thursday in a WeChat post that it has raised more than $500 million, the company’s first funding round since Meta was forced to call off its $2 billion acquisition of the startup.
Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led the funding round, and existing shareholders Tencent, HSG (formerly known as Sequoia China), ZhenFund, and others also participated.
Manus did not disclose its valuation, but last month was said to be in talks with investors to raise $500 million at a $4 billion valuation.
why_it_matters_hint: Manus found $500 million of new funding without Meta, after Beijing blocked the sale.
notes: Reuters original blocked (401). TechCrunch and The Next Web carry the same announcement (company WeChat post). Valuation not disclosed.
